calendar_legend: one dot = one event that day
communities_ctaBody: A name, a link and where you publish your events. From then on we import them twice a day.
communities_intro: Who organises what, and how often. If one is missing, open a report: we usually add it within a few days.
communities_metaDescription: Who runs events in {city} and its province: tech, design, culture, business and social. An open list, maintained by the communities themselves.
community_metaFallback: {name}: events, rhythm and contacts. {count} events coming up in {city}.
community_noUpcoming: Nothing scheduled at the moment. We check the sources twice a day: as soon as they publish, it shows up here on its own.
eventPage_dataSource: Imported from the community’s public pages. Something off? {#link to=$report}Report it{/link}.
eventPage_pastNotice: This event has already taken place. We keep it online as the community’s archive.
eventPage_registrationHint: Registration happens on the community’s own site. We do not handle tickets here.
footer_license: Code {#link to=$code}AGPL-3.0{/link}, {#link to=$data}data ODbL 1.0{/link}. Maps © {#link to=$osm}OpenStreetMap{/link} contributors.
home_communitiesCta: Who organises what, and how often. If one is missing, a name and a link are enough — we take it from there.
home_empty: Nothing scheduled right now. The crawlers check the sources twice a day; if you are organising something, {#link to=$submit}tell us about it{/link}.
home_emptyFiltered: No events match the filters you picked.
home_intro: Events from the communities of the city and the province. We are a mirror: tickets and sign-ups stay where they already are.
howto_apple1: On iPhone, iPad or Mac, press "Subscribe" above and confirm.
howto_apple2: On a Mac you can also use File → New Calendar Subscription, then paste the address.
howto_browseCalendar: Month calendar: a dot marks a day with events. Tap it to see only that day.
howto_browseFilters: Filters: above the list you can narrow by period, area, cost and topic. "Reset" clears them all.
howto_browseMap: Map: each pin carries the number of its event in the list.
howto_browseRegistration: Registration and tickets stay on the organiser's site: every event links there.
howto_formatsBody: The same events are also an {#link to=$rss}RSS feed{/link}, for news readers, and {#link to=$json}JSON data{/link}, for anyone who wants to build on them.
howto_google1: Open Google Calendar on a computer: the phone app cannot add a calendar from a link.
howto_google2: In the left column, next to "Other calendars", press + and choose "From URL".
howto_google3: Paste the address and press "Add calendar". It then shows up on your phone too.
howto_intro: We gather the events the communities publish into one place, twice a day. You can browse them here, or bring them into the calendar you already use, with nothing to remember to check.
howto_metaDescription: How to follow community events in {city}: subscribe to the calendar, add a single event, browse the agenda.
howto_missingBody: We read the communities' public pages twice a day. If a community is not here, {#link to=$submit}suggest it{/link}; for a one-off event, {#link to=$event}submit the event{/link}; if something is wrong, {#link to=$fix}send a correction{/link}.
howto_other1: Thunderbird, Proton Calendar, DAVx⁵ and nearly every other app accept a calendar from a link: look for "subscribe" or "from URL" and paste the address.
howto_outlook1: On Outlook.com or Outlook on the web: Calendar → Add calendar → Subscribe from web.
howto_outlook2: Paste the address, give the calendar a name and import it.
howto_refreshNote: Each app decides how often to check again: Apple usually within a few hours, Google sometimes only after a day. If an event that just appeared here is not in your calendar yet, that is normal.
howto_singleBody: Only interested in one? Open the event page and, under "Add to calendar", choose:
howto_singleGoogle: Google: opens Google Calendar with the event already filled in, just save it.
howto_singleIcs: .ics: downloads a file that opens in Apple Calendar, Outlook and most other apps.
howto_singleNote: It is a copy: if the time or place changes later, your calendar will not know. To stay up to date, subscribe instead.
howto_subscribeBody: The easiest way. Add the calendar once and it keeps itself up to date: new events, changed times, cancellations.
map_noScript: The map needs JavaScript. Every event is listed next to it anyway.

match.countPlural=one: {count} event without a location on the map
match.countPlural=other: {count} events without a location on the map

notFound_body: It might be an event removed at the source, or a mistyped address. Past events stay online, so if you were after something old it should still be there.
submitEvent_fieldCommunityHelp: Every event is credited to whoever organises it. Pick one from the list, or type the name if it is not there yet.
submitEvent_fieldCommunityUrl: Community website, if it is not listed yet
submitEvent_fieldCommunityUrlHelp: Only for a new community: we add it together with the event.
submitEvent_fieldTopicsHelp: Leave them empty to use the community's own.
submitEvent_fieldUrlHelp: The organiser's page, where people sign up. This site is only a mirror: without a page to send people to we cannot list it.
submitEvent_intro: For an event you cannot find in the calendar: a hackathon, a conference, a one-off talk. If the community publishes events regularly, {#link to=$community}add the community{/link} instead: then we import them on our own.
submitEvent_metaDescription: Submit an event to the {city} calendar: title, date, event page and who organises it.
submitEvent_next3: Once merged, the event is live after the next collection run, within half a day.
submitEvent_recurringBody: If the community organises often, adding it is better: its events arrive on their own, with no need to submit them one by one.
submit_buttonIssue: I would rather open an issue
submit_contactHelp: This ends up in a public GitHub issue along with the rest. Leave it blank if you would rather stay anonymous.
submit_eventBody: A hackathon, a conference, a one-off talk: if the community does not publish events regularly, submitting that one is enough.
submit_eventsHelp: This is the part that matters most. If you have an .ics feed or a page on gdg.community.dev, Luma, Gancio or Mobilizon, we read it automatically. Meetup and Eventbrite have closed their APIs, so those we copy by hand.
submit_failedLink: Open the issue on GitHub with your answers already filled in →
submit_fieldContactPlaceholder: Only if you want a reply
submit_fieldTaglinePlaceholder: What you do, in a few words
submit_fixBody: Wrong date, changed venue, cancelled event: open a correction and we fix it by hand — corrections take precedence over the crawlers.
submit_githubNote: We take you to the GitHub form with your answers already filled in: you need a GitHub account, and from there you just confirm.
submit_intro: A name, a link and where you publish your events. From then on we import them twice a day, with nothing for you to remember.
submit_metaDescription: Add your community to the {city} events calendar: a name, a link and where you publish your events.
submit_next1: Your report becomes a public issue on the repository.
submit_next2: An automation turns it into a pull request with the file ready to go.
submit_next3: Once merged, the community is live and its events start arriving on their own.
submit_nextHint: It all happens in the open: no private moderation, the whole history is in the repository.
submit_noScript: This form needs JavaScript. You can still {#link to=$issue}open an issue on GitHub{/link}, which is exactly what the form does for you.
submit_ok: Done, thanks. Your report has been recorded.
submit_okWithLink: Done. Your report is now a public issue — the link is below.
